target.numbering: E. coli MurJ wild-type numbering. The construct used for the structures is EcMurJ(5-500) with an N-terminal BRIL fusion, so PDB residues 1-4 (KYLL, present in all three models and covalently linked to residue 5) are the fusion linker, NOT MurJ, and are excluded from every analysis. BRIL itself is numbered -101..0. MurJ therefore contributes exactly 496 residues (5-500).

reference.citation: Li Y.E., Antillon S.F., Baron G.F., Chamakura K., Young R., Clemons W.M. Jr. Convergent MurJ flippase inhibition by phage lysis proteins. Nature 652, 1274-1280 (2026).

structures.note: Cryo-EM. SglM packs tightly against TM2 and TM7, mainly through hydrophobic interactions.
Cryo-EM. Glu96 bridges Lys46/Arg270; C-terminal helix lies in the central cavity.

_doc_verify_types.salt_bridge: MurJ residue must form a salt bridge (<= cutoff) to a peptide Asp/Glu carboxylate or to the peptide C-terminal OXT.
_doc_verify_types.buried_contact: MurJ residue must contact the peptide in >= min_complexes structures AND lose >= min_dsasa A^2 of SASA upon peptide binding.
_doc_verify_types.peptide_salt_bridge: Peptide residue must form a salt bridge to one of the listed MurJ residues.
_doc_verify_types.peptide_contact: Peptide residue must make >= min_atoms heavy-atom contacts with MurJ.

murj_residues.claim: Lys46 sits in the hydrophilic central cavity, is essential for flippase activity, and is the anchor that acidic Sgl residues reach.
murj_residues.quote: Both Lys46 and Arg270 are located in the hydrophilic central cavity and are essential for flippase activity in E. coli
murj_residues.locator: Results, convergent features of Sgl-MurJ complexes; Fig. 4d,e

murj_residues.claim: Arg53 is functionally important, forms a coevolving pair with Glu273 that stabilises the squeezed state, and contacts the C-terminal carboxylate of SglPP7 and SglCJ3.
murj_residues.quote: Arg53-Glu273 is a coevolving pair that stabilizes the squeezed form of MurJ

murj_residues.claim: Arg270 is essential, is proposed to bind the lipid II diphosphate, and rotates to bridge Glu96 of SglCJ3.
murj_residues.quote: Arg270 has been proposed to bind the diphosphate of the lipid II head group

murj_residues.claim: Lys368 forms a thin gate with the conserved G/A-E-G-A motif and contacts the C-terminal carboxylate of the peptides.
murj_residues.quote: Lys368 forms a thin gate with the conserved G/A-E-G-A motif to occlude the bound lipid II

resistance_mutations.claim: Leu50 maps to the SglCJ3-MurJ interface and contacts both SglCJ3 helices; Trp substitution is sterically incompatible with peptide binding.
resistance_mutations.quote: The SglCJ3-resistant mutant Leu50Trp in MurJ TM2 occurs at the SglCJ3-MurJ interface, contacting both helices of SglCJ3
resistance_mutations.locator: Results, structure of MurJ bound to SglCJ3; Fig. 3

resistance_mutations.claim: Gln244 was the first SglPP7 resistance allele; it lies at the TM2/TM7 groove and is contacted by the peptides.
resistance_mutations.quote: a point mutant in MurJ (Q244P) conferred resistance to SglPP7-mediated lysis. This mutation also provides resistance to SglM

unverifiable_claims.claim: Thirteen of the residues in MurJ that Sgls contact are completely conserved across diderms.
unverifiable_claims.quote: Thirteen of the residues in MurJ that Sgls contact are completely conserved across diderms
unverifiable_claims.why_not_verified: Requires a multiple sequence alignment over diderm MurJ orthologues, which is not part of this repository. Note that 13 is a SEQUENCE-conservation count; it is not the same quantity as the geometric convergence count computed here (residues contacting the peptide in all three deposited structures).

unverifiable_claims.claim: Sgls stall the lipid II transport cycle by trapping MurJ in an outward-facing (periplasm-open) state.
unverifiable_claims.why_not_verified: A conformational claim. This repository measures the peptide-bound state only; state selectivity must be tested downstream against an inward-facing structure.
